correctness.rationale: PASS: Direct differentiation verifies ψ(x,y)=(1/(x+y),y/[x(x+y)]) is involutive with signed determinant -1/[x²(x+y)²], so the gain-map Jacobian is its absolute j=1/[x²(x+y)²]. The energy x+y+1/x and ratio y/x invariants and monomial Jacobian show GIG(p,c)⊗Gamma(p,c) product q is exactly invariant under density pushforward K. The loss/gain marginal equations yield F'=∫(Kg-g)log(g/q)=-KL(g||Kg) and H'=F'-E_g log j. At perturbed product gε=q(1+εh(x)), h(x)=x/(1+x)-E_qX[x/(1+x)] is bounded smooth increasing; m(x)=E_qY log j(x,Y) is strictly decreasing since m'=-2/x-2E(1/(x+Y))<0. Thus B=-Cov_qX(h,m)>0. The KL defect ≤4ε²/(1-ε); for sufficiently small ε>0, H'(0)=εB-KL>0 for every p,c>0. Independent symbolic involution, Jacobian, invariance checks verify the algebra; sign proof is analytic, not numerical. Relative-entropy identity is not a convergence-rate theorem.
